title: Directed Evolution
description: A million generations in a minute, if time runs fast enough. Unlocks the Evolution Engine and telomerase.

puzzle.goal: A new mutant with selective advantage s appears in a population of N, starting at frequency p. Random drift and selection act together; in the diffusion limit the chance it ever takes over is a ratio of two integrals of the same weight function, which decays exponentially with the frequency x at rate 4Ns.
puzzle.name: Kimura fixation probability (diffusion approximation)
puzzle.form: int ( 0 , p , exp ( - 4 * N * s * x ) , x ) / int ( 0 , 1 , exp ( - 4 * N * s * x ) , x )
puzzle.ask: The integrals give (1 − e^(−4Nsp)) / (1 − e^(−4Ns)). Find the fixation probability of a single new mutant, p = 1/(2N).
puzzle.method: Solve the backward diffusion equation with absorbing boundaries at 0 and 1: the solution is the integral of exp(−2∫M/V) from 0 to p, normalised by the same integral to 1.
